module_title: Recent Important Amendments (100th to 106th) - Basic Understanding
introduction: In recent years, the Indian Parliament has passed several landmark constitutional amendments that have reshaped taxation, reservations, and women's representation. Memorizing the most recent amendments (from 100 to 106) is absolutely crucial for current affairs and polity sections of any competitive exam.

core_concepts.title: 101st Amendment (2016) - GST
core_concepts.description: Introduced the Goods and Services Tax (GST). It replaced multiple indirect taxes levied by the State and Central governments with a single, unified national tax.

core_concepts.title: 103rd Amendment (2019) - EWS Quota
core_concepts.description: Introduced a 10% reservation for the Economically Weaker Sections (EWS) among the unreserved (General) category in government jobs and educational institutions.

core_concepts.title: 106th Amendment (2023) - Women's Reservation
core_concepts.description: Officially known as the 'Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam'. It mandates a 33% (one-third) reservation for women in the Lok Sabha, State Legislative Assemblies, and the Delhi Assembly.

important_entities.name: Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam
important_entities.significance: This is the most recent and highly tested amendment. It aims to significantly boost women's political representation at the state and national levels.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A massive trap! Not all Constitutional Amendment Bills become Acts. For example, the Women's Reservation Bill was the 128th Constitutional Amendment BILL, but after passing, it became the 106th Constitutional Amendment ACT. Exams will try to confuse you with these two numbers.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: In India, giving 101 rupees is considered auspicious. Remember 101 as the 'financial gift' of GST to the nation's economy.

exam_strategy_tips: Always link 101 to GST, 103 to EWS, and 106 to Women's Reservation. These three are the highest-yield recent amendments for any objective exam.
